interpretation: Choices follow the order the image sheets appeared: companions, harbor-friends, keepers-town, reef-hosts, harbor-residents. The turtle at position 11 is Mira; the user separately clarified a teenage redesign. Columns 1/2/3 correspond to A/B/C.

shelly.status: Included in current expression concept review; existing game asset unchanged until review is resolved.

sharedDirection.style: Organically sculpted 3D storybook marine characters, cohesive with approved Shelly.
sharedDirection.individuality: Distinct silhouettes, eye and brow shapes, expressions, ages, posture, work accessories, materials and movement personalities.
sharedDirection.tone: The cast must not all look dreamy or ethereal. Use grounded textures and role-appropriate colors. Reserve subtle bioluminescence and pearlescence for characters where it belongs.
constraints: No universal gold filigree, sparkles or iridescence
Final models must match their references from viewable angles
sharedDirection.paletteCorrection: The third revised cast sheet was rejected for repeating green/pink colors and similar expressions. Echo, Pip, Jisu, the town shopkeeper, taxi driver and subway guide need visibly separate palettes and facial acting while sharing modeling, materials and rendering style.
sharedDirection.paletteRule: Thoughtfully choose animal colors from real biological references and use occupational colors in clothing/accessories. Preserve the improved differentiated shapes/expressions. Avoid a cast-wide yellow/brown or green/pink scheme.
sharedDirection.eyeStyle: Expressive A eyes from natural-survey sheets, preferred across whole cast.
sharedDirection.mouths: Remove human-like smiles. Use species-specific mouths/mouthparts and role-appropriate facial reactions; see expression-review/manifest.json.
sharedDirection.expressionReview: A-eye and natural mouth direction accepted for development, with explicit personality-dependent eye acting across the cast.
sharedDirection.eyePerformance: Each personality shapes eye expressions: resting gaze, eyelid pose where suitable, gaze shifts, response timing and species-appropriate stalk/head/bell motion. A defines the eye design; dialogue and emotion drive changing eye acting.

characters.customDirection: A teenage turtle. Keep the design family similar to Shelly, with an obviously different color theme and teenager-appropriate accessories. Younger than an adult storyteller, visibly older than baby Shelly.
characters.implementationDirection: Selected teenage concept3:seafoam and cream skin, slate-blue/sage shell, forehead goggles, coral canvas map satchel, youthful confident expression; keep Shelly unchanged.

Selected Echo3 beluga: round pearl-white/cool-gray body, recognizable melon forehead, no dorsal fin, horizontal tail flukes, gentle confident face and cobalt-blue side satchel. Supersedes the nautilus and the brief Echo1 bottlenose selection.

Selected Pip2 royal gramma: violet-purple front half, golden-yellow rear/tail, lively mischievous expression, mint/cream puzzle notebook; natural fish body, fins and vertical tail, no human hands or legs. Supersedes the cuttlefish.

characters.accessories: Tangerine-orange postal pouch and orange scallop-shell envelope seal.
characters.movement: Quick scuttle with brief blue-white electrical speed cues, skipped in Calm Motion.

characters.ability: Intentionally change skin among natural ruby, harbor stone camouflage and cream/maroon display; keep apron and eyes unchanged.
characters.anatomy: Exactly eight separate unbranched arms, each originating at the body and ending in one tip. No merged or tip-to-tip connections. All eight tips clearly visible in the corrected concept; verify actual 3D geometry from several angles before activation.

characters.expression: Bored: half-lidded eyes, relaxed low brows, short flat closed mouth, slouched unhurried posture. No smile or smirk.

characters.scale: Dominant wide-bodied marine organism; substantially larger than the octopus and tiny Jisu. Camera adapts to wingspan.

status: A-eye visual direction accepted for ongoing development; distinct personality-dependent eye acting required. Body/accessory refinements and finished-model validation continue.
